extracted.intended_audience: social media editors, newsroom managers, and newsroom staff who post or set policy for newsroom social accounts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for newsroom decisions about what to share on social media and how to present it across platforms; functions as a real-time newsworthiness rubric for social sharing. Covers account conduct, shareable vs. non-shareable content, format and topic signals that perform on social, per-platform tactics, and implicit editorial/algorithmic filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsroom Account Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: "Treat each post as your own" — if newsroom wouldn't write it, don't repost
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major breaking stories: official accounts go first. Reporter accounts can amplify with own commentary. Link to developing stories. Overall standard: posts from newsroom accounts should reflect editorial standards and the newsroom voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original reporting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority share; emphasizes proprietary reporting as core shareable content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking news with verification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share breaking events only once verification standards are met; verify before amplifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis pieces
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label analysis clearly so audiences can distinguish reporting from interpretation or opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-form features repurposed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repurpose or excerpt long-form work for social distribution, using compelling hooks or visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live event coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social for real-time reporting and live updates; indicate live status when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual content
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize strong visual assets to increase engagement and clarity; use captions and sourcing for visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share interactive content to engage audiences, gather input, and build community while maintaining editorial integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behind-the-scenes (limited)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sparingly to humanize coverage but avoid revealing sensitive editorial processes or undermining trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unverified breaking news (do not share)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not repost or amplify breaking claims without verification; prioritize accuracy over speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partisan commentary (do not share)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid posting content that reads as partisan advocacy from newsroom accounts; maintain neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal political views (from work account) (do not share)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff should not use newsroom accounts to express personal political opinions; separate personal accounts if appropriate and follow disclosure practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disparaging advertisers or competitors (do not share)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid posts that attack or disparage advertisers, commercial partners, or competitors to protect editorial independence and commercial relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disparaging readers (do not share)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain respectful tone toward audiences; do not post content that insults or demeans readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anything undermining editorial integrity (do not share)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid posts that could create conflicts of interest, suggest bias, reveal confidential sourcing, or otherwise weaken trust in the newsroom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short, punchy sentences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise, attention-grabbing copy for social; favors readability and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong visual asset
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair copy with compelling visuals (photo, chart, video) to increase distribution and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote-able core fact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with a specific, quotable fact or statistic that summarizes the story's key point for easy sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-intuitive finding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight surprising or counter-intuitive elements to provoke curiosity and clicks, while ensuring accuracy and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outrage-inducing (use carefully)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content that provokes outrage can drive engagement but should be used cautiously to avoid sensationalism or harm to trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise / delight factor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that inspire delight or wonder can perform well; use this angle responsibly and authentically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emoji-friendly subject
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider emoji usage where appropriate to signal tone or capture attention, aligned with brand voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics: Breaking events
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real-world breaking events are highly shareable when verified and timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics: Controversial opinions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controversial takes can trend, but ensure appropriate labeling (op-ed/analysis) and context to avoid misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics: Visual spectacle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eye-catching visuals or dramatic scenes tend to perform well on social platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics: Outrage-bait politics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political content that incites anger trends, but newsrooms should avoid amplifying manipulative or misleading political content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics: Celebrity moments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Celebrity-related content drives attention; verify sources and avoid gossip that violates standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics: Sports outcomes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely sports results and highlights perform well—use quick updates and visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics: Cultural memes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memes and cultural references can increase reach; ensure they align with brand tone and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics: Inspirational stories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive, human-interest stories can drive shares and community goodwill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twitter / X considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Twitter / X: Real-time breaking; threading for context; replies/quote tweets engagement; verified-author boost
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use threads to add context; engage via replies and quote tweets; leverage verified authors to increase visibility for breaking coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facebook considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Facebook: Algorithm favors comments and shares; video performs well; local groups relevant for local news; Less reach for news pages (post-2018 changes)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage conversation to trigger algorithmic distribution; prioritize video and local group strategies for reach; be aware of page reach limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instagram considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Instagram: Visual-first (image, video, reels, stories); Less news-friendly historically; Carousel format for explainers; Stories for ephemeral
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use high-quality visuals, carousels for explainers, and stories/reels for short-form or ephemeral updates; adapt tone for Instagram's audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: TikTok considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok: Short video; Vertical format; Music / trending sounds; Younger audience; Hook in first 3 seconds
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create vertical short-form videos with strong opening hooks, use trending sounds where appropriate, and tailor content to younger demographics.

rubrics_metrics.name: YouTube considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube: Long-form video; Searchable; Title/thumbnail crucial; Watch-time matters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize titles and thumbnails; structure videos for watch-time retention and search discoverability; favor longer-form explainers or recorded segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: LinkedIn considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: LinkedIn: Professional / business audience; Thought leadership; Industry analysis; Career news
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post industry-focused analysis, career-related reporting, and thought leadership tailored to a professional audience and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform-fit format
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a story's format and assets match the norms and constraints of the target platform before posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic favorability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predict and optimize for platform algorithms (e.g., favoring video, engagement signals, watch-time) when deciding what and how to post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement prediction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate likely engagement (likes/comments/shares) and choose stories and formats with higher engagement potential, while balancing editorial values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand-appropriate tone
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain tone consistent with newsroom brand across platforms; avoid off-brand stunts or language that could harm reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-zone optimization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule posts to align with audience time zones and peak engagement windows for maximum reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hashtag strategy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hashtags strategically to reach relevant audiences without appearing spammy; platform norms vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-post avoidance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid blindly cross-posting identical content across platforms; adapt format, copy, and assets for each platform's norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-segment targeting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor posts to distinct audience segments (local vs. national, younger vs. older) and choose platforms/content accordingly.
